_comment: The cross-language contract fixture (§35 C4c, plan-conf-duplication.md D3): wire-riding values that Go and the client both restate by hand. Each side asserts its own table against this file — Go: backend/cmd/aurad/shared_constants_test.go (plus backend/pkg/aura/skills/shared_constants_test.go for the skill vocabularies, whose Go maps are unexported), client: frontend/src/client-data/SharedConstants.test.ts — so a drift goes red on whichever side moved. Contract only (names ↔ values); colors, styles and pixel scaling stay client-side. Not loaded by the game: tests read it from the repo, so it needs no cp-defs/embed entry.
_skillPointCostComment: The D10 escalating point curve (plan-numbers-rewrite): buying a level costs `tier1Points` while the level is within the first `tier2AboveFraction` of the skill's OWN cap, `tier2Points` up to `tier3AboveFraction`, `tier3Points` beyond — thresholds rounded UP. Level 1 is free on unlock, so the first purchased level is 2. Cross-language because the client shows the cost on the spellbook + button. ⚑ Every value is [PLACEHOLDER], the fractions included.
_hpRoundingComment: vitals.HP, the rule every absolute health amount passes through before it is dealt: round half up to a whole point, and never round a positive amount away to nothing (min 1). R1/F6 puts it in TypeScript for the first time — the skill tooltip now shows a cost in absolute HP, so client and server must round the SAME fraction to the SAME point or the tooltip promises a price the server does not charge. Stated as input → output pairs rather than as prose, because a rule restated in two languages is exactly the drift class §35 closed. Go: model/vitals.HP. Client: roundHP in client-data/Skills.ts.
_costChargeTriggerComment: WHEN an aura effect's cost is taken, which is not the same question as how often the effect fires. R2 (plan-resource-costs-feedback §5.2) made five of the seven chargeable types pay only for work DONE: they report new-vs-refresh out of the buff store and are charged off that answer, so holding one on a target set that is not changing is free. Only damage_aura and heal_aura still pay on every application, and only they can honestly print a cadence on their cost line. Cross-language because BOTH sides restate it: the client picks the cost line's wording (SkillTooltip.ts COST_TRIGGER_TEXT) and the Go content guard picks which effects the haste term applies to (cmd/aurad workGatedCharge). ⚑ The real authority is what each applier RETURNS in sys/skills.go — this file cannot derive that, it can only stop the two restatements drifting apart from each other. A new chargeable type must be added here, and both sides then fail until they agree.
_pointsPerMeterComment: The world-scale factor: meters (backend units) per pixel-point (client units). Go: codec.Points2px (codec/minions.go), applied to every wire position. Client: PIXEL_PER_METER / meter2px in client-data/BasicConfig.ts. If the two ever split, every entity renders at the wrong world scale with nothing failing (plan-code-health.md C4).
_utilityCastTicksComment: Cast durations of the three baseline utilities, in ticks (plan-code-health.md C4 / D4: pinned, not served — a /utilities endpoint for three deliberately-outside-the-catalog entries fails KISS/YAGNI, recorded so nobody re-litigates). Go: skills/utility.go utilityDefs CastTicks. Client: UTILITY_CAST_SECONDS (Utilities.ts) derives its seconds from these ticks over ticksPerSecond, purely for the tooltip. All values [PLACEHOLDER].
_activeAuraSlotComment: The active_aura_slot wire sentinels — one contract, two restatements. -1 is the FlatBuffers schema default ('no aura command this input'); -2 is the wire-only workaround for FlatBuffers omitting a scalar equal to its default, which makes an explicit -1 indistinguishable from an absent field. Drift makes aura deactivation a silent no-op. Go: model/input.go ActiveAuraSlotNoChange/ActiveAuraSlotDeactivate. Client: InputMessage.ts NO_ACTIVE_AURA_CHANGE/DEACTIVATE_AURA_SLOT. Collapse -2 onto -1 (here and on both sides) if the schema default is ever changed and regenerated.
_playerColliderRadiusComment: The player body's physical collider radius in meters. Go: player.ColliderRadiusMeters (model/player/player.go). Client: Graphics.ts colliderRadiusMeters (aura-ring extension math) and the character sprite size derived from it. Not on the wire — the server never sends the player's own radius — so both sides own the number.
_apiErrorCodesComment: The accounts API's refusal codes, verbatim string twins (plan-code-health.md C4, research-code-quality §11.3 F3). Go: the code* consts in accounts/respond.go (unexported, so the pin test lives in that package). Client: API_ERROR_CODES in AccountsApi.ts, which branches UI flow on them — a renamed code degrades every branch to the generic error path with nothing failing. The client-only 'network' (the request never got a reply) is deliberately NOT in this list.
_campChargeCapComment: How many Camp charges a character can hold (plan-downtime.md D9): `base` at level 1, one more every `perLevels` levels — cap = base + floor(level / perLevels). D9's reasoning: the camp's heal is %-of-max, so its strength already scales with the pool for free; COUNT is the axis that would otherwise be flat, and it is the one the player can see grow. Cross-language because the cap is deliberately NOT a wire field — the server sends the live charge count and the client derives the cap from the level it already knows (getLocalPlayerLevel), so the button can read `2/3` without a second field. Go: skills.CampChargeCap. Client: campChargeCap in client-data/Skills.ts. ⚑ Both values [PLACEHOLDER] — retuned 2026-08-03 after the PO's first hand pass, from 3 / +1-per-10 to 1 / +1-per-7: 1 charge at level 1, 2 from level 7, 3 from level 14, topping out at 5 by level 30. The first curve was generous enough that a level-1 character never ran out, which made the walk back to a fire optional and the whole loop invisible.
_skillVocabularyComment: UI pass C8 (plan-ui-pass.md §5 C8): the four content-keyed vocabularies the skill tooltip restates by hand in label tables and `case` clauses. Go: skills.effectTypeMap / selectorMap / GateKeys / validStats (unexported, so the pin test lives in pkg/aura/skills/shared_constants_test.go - the accounts-codes precedent). Client: SkillTooltip.ts effectBlock() cases + EFFECT_COLOR_KEYS + TICKING_TYPES (effectTypes), SELECTOR_LABELS (selectors; `all` is phrased by the targets line, not the table), GATE_KEY_LINES (gateKeys), STAT_LABELS (statNames). Exhaustive both directions on each side, so a new type/selector/key/stat fails vitest or go test until the tooltip has decided what to say about it. ⚑ The selector list omits the `""` alias: it parses as nearest but is not a name (catalog.go reverseNames skips it). costChargeTrigger's key set above is separately pinned == TICKING_TYPES.
